confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly reports random allocation of new employers between June 7 and July 20, 2023, to treatment or the status quo control. Randomization occurs at the employer-account level on the first posting attempt and persists on subsequent attempts; the reported allocations are 90,048 treated and 90,276 control accounts.

S1 assigns an offer of assistance, not compulsory use: treated employers choose whether to use AI, and control employers receive the standard posting flow. This confirms the form's platform-feature comparison without asserting that off-platform AI use was absent.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.1; p. 37, Section 8, randomized holdout description; p. 38, first paragraph, possible diffusion of off-platform AI use.

confirmed.statement: S1 supplies generative assistance for the employer's own work: a short prompt produces a job-post draft, required skills, and a category. Employers can edit or discard the text and request casual, formal, shorter, more detailed, or rewritten versions before posting.
S1 uptake and editing details match the form: the prose reports 75% taking up the draft and 66% posting it without edits; Table 21 separately reports an opt-in mean of 0.752 with 27,111 observations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, last paragraph; p. 12, Section 4.1; p. 56, Table 21, Opt-in rate for AI feature.

confirmed.statement: S1 text comparisons condition on posting. The paper acknowledges that conditional estimates can combine changes in the composition of posters with effects of AI-written text, consistent with the form's caveat about full-sample intention-to-treat interpretation.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14, Figure 2 notes and Section 4.4; p. 24, Section 6, discussion following equation (2); p. 47, Table 12 notes.

confirmed.statement: S2 explicitly reports random allocation of returning employers between April 20 and June 6, 2023. Subsequent jobs by a treated employer retain treatment, supporting assignment between employers rather than a crossover design.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 66, Appendix B, second paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S2 offers an optional AI-generated description after title, expected duration, skills, and budget have been entered. Those inputs form a prompt to a generative AI service; control employers type their own descriptions, and employers declining AI see that same manual page.
S2 assistance is used to produce employers' own job descriptions, which they can edit. The form's 53% uptake and 78% editing among opt-ins are explicitly reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 71, Section B.3 and Table 35.

confirmed.statement: S3 explicitly expands access to the same AI drafting feature to 95% of new employers and retains a randomized 5% holdout without access. Figure 15 confirms random assignment and the October 10, 2023 to February 18, 2024 sample period.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 37, Section 8, first paragraph; p. 68, Figure 15 notes.

confirmed.statement: The drafting service is explicitly generative but its provider and model are not named. OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 measures semantic similarity, and GPT4o scores prompt informativeness; neither is identified as the intervention model.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.1 and empty footnote 12; p. 14, footnote 14; p. 48, Figure 10 notes; p. 69, Section B.2.

confirmed.statement: S1-S3 compare treatment and control employers, with no assigned within-person sequence of AI and no-AI conditions. Randomization of condition order is therefore not applicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3; p. 66, Appendix B; p. 37, Section 8; p. 68, Figure 15 notes.

confirmed.statement: S4 is correctly recorded as observational: editing is chosen by treated employers who opted into the draft, and the authors explicitly acknowledge selection as an explanation for edited-versus-unedited differences.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 17, continuation of Section 4.5.2; p. 50, Table 15 notes.

confirmed.statement: The saved document reports no preregistration for these experiments, consistent with the form's not_stated entries.
confirmed.locator: Complete saved document, PDF pp. 1-72, including Appendices A-B; design descriptions on pp. 9, 37, and 66-69.

summary: The PDF explicitly reports random assignment to generative-AI drafting access versus standard posting in S1, S2, and S3. Criterion 1 holds at the employer-account level, and S4 is correctly coded as a nonrandomized editing comparison.
